      "observations": [
        "All 620 owned diff lines across 21 paths were read. The new mailnews_string_glue crate exports nfc_normalize through a C header and both Rust linkage crates. DatabaseUtils::Normalize changes from the temporary byte-preserving bypass to Result<nsCString, nsresult>; changed folder, message and migration callers use MOZ_TRY. A normalization failure returns before the affected later statement execution. This does not prove whole-migration rollback or database transaction atomicity.",
        "The Rust bridge rejects null pointers, but its safety contract separately requires valid allocated and distinct nsACString instances. The local SAFETY comments mention only non-nullness and could name that stronger caller contract. The destination receives the normalized head before a possible tail-write error; C++ uses a separate local destination and returns Err rather than exposing a successful string on failure. Invalid UTF-8 and allocation behavior inside the dependency remain unpaired.",
        "The patch re-enables selected decomposed root lookup, duplicate-folder, child/path lookup, sender/subject, Bcc and migrated-recipient expectations. Sender/subject helper assertions have expected-behavior messages. Newly active lookup, relations, Bcc and migration assertions lack messages, as does the changed MOZ_ASSERT. This is a scoped assertion-message finding; absence of should alone is not a defect. No Rust null/error-path test is added.",
        "Fixed accepted Rust and C++ retain this bridge and error propagation. The exact backout later reverses all 21 paths, and the separate reland restores the same functional bodies. Cargo metadata is build registration, not handwritten style evidence. The incidental nsDBFolderInfo constructor reflow is not a new behavior. No test, build or native Unicode execution ran.",
        "The complete original primary 2019183 was read once for the original/backout/reland family. It distinguishes initial local-build failure, temporary bypass, original normalization landing, explicit build-bustage backout, then reland. Its proposed Rust snippet is a suggestion rather than the landed implementation. Full D284928 has 14 actual inline bodies and no summary edits, including discussion after the original landing.",
        "The landed C header adopts extern C linkage. The Rust source adopts the requested Safety section, valid allocated distinct-pointer condition, direct src_ref argument and is_err branch. The validity inline remains Not Done, so badges do not determine adoption. Local unsafe comments still explain only nullness and could state the full caller contract. The reviewer identifies an unused ICU dependency in mailnews_ui_glue; author agrees it is a leftover, while the original lock still carries that entry and the reland removes it.",
        "The dedicated string crate is justified as separation from user-facing UI glue and preparation for possible string/ICU work, a scoped architectural decision rather than a global crate rule. Review discussion says sink errors may be impossible and later clarifies that normalization forwards sink errors. The author retains interface error handling. Dependency bodies were not independently checked here, so the new Result lesson is conditional code flow, not a claim that malformed input reaches that error path. The author transaction-abort explanation is historical; whole-migration atomicity is not proven.",
        "The stray blank-line request is reflected in the landed migration hunk; the incidental constructor reflow is acknowledged as clang-format output and remains unrelated to Unicode behavior. Historical rustfmt failures, subsequent remote completions and Try locators are not fresh verification. Re-enabled assertion scopes and missing messages remain as recorded in the source packet."
